thread:
maria gonzalez: Quick sync — thinking about adding an "inline policy template" option for automatic fallback. lightweight, composable, and versioned. thoughts?

jen lee: +1 on versioning. we need an easy dry-run mode so SRE can sanity-check behavior before it affects traffic.

samir patel: agree on dry-run. Also we should support a simple priority list: primary model -> cheaper fallback -> canned response. Keep it human-readable in console.

kevin chen: UX nit: when dry-run is on, console should show 'simulated decisions' with a clear badge and a link to the exact inputs used. Otherwise people will assume it's live.

maria gonzalez: good call. What about triggers? error-code-based, latency-threshold, token-cost-spike, or custom predicate?

tariq ahmed: prefer enum + custom predicate. default presets: "error-5xx", "latency-95p>500ms", "qps-surge". custom predicates could be JS-ish or CEL.

jen lee: CEL would be safer than full JS. We already evaluate CEL elsewhere for routing.

samir patel: +1 CEL. Also we should include a small sample-rate for fallback to avoid oscillation on noisy errors (eg. fallback_rate: 0.2).

maria gonzalez: sample-rate is good. UX question: how do we present the audit trail? operators want an easy way to see "why" a request was downgraded.

kevin chen: show the evaluation stack for each decision id: trigger matched, predicate result, sampling roll, model chosen, and sketch of KV/cache hit. Link each decision to a trace id. UI should redact user tokens but keep signal context.

maria gonzalez: perfect. We should also store the policy-version and dry-run flag in the audit row. That helps playback.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: policy-service v2.14 -> staging (rollout: canary 5%)

tariq ahmed: for the console templates, propose three modes: "conservative" (fail-open to fallback), "aggressive" (fail-close, reject), "stepped" (multi-tier fallback). Each template should expose knobs: sampling, TTL backoff, cooldown window.

jen lee: UI layout idea: top-level policy editor with YAML/visual toggle, a small test harness panel (input + trace), and a recent-decisions table with filters (model, trigger, user tenant).

samir patel: on TTL backoff — add jitter to window to avoid synchronized switchover of multi-tenant apps.

maria gonzalez: Let's put a guardrail: minimum audit retention of 30d for enterprise customers, with opt-out for dev orgs. Also metric emission for: fallback_rate, mean_latency_post_fallback, pct_errors_by_trigger.

kevin chen: API side: expose /policies/{id}/evaluate with optional ?dry_run=true that returns the chosen action + explanation. Useful for integration tests. Rate-limit it.

jen lee: example inline template to prototype in console (displayed in editor):
```yaml
version: 1
name: small-service-starter
triggers:
  - id: latency_95p
    type: latency_percentile
    threshold_ms: 500
actions:
  - id: fallback_a
    type: route_to_model
    model: cheap-2b-quant
    sample_rate: 0.25
  - id: canned
    type: canned_response
    content_key: "grace_reply_v1"
backoff:
  ttl_seconds: 300
  jitter_pct: 10
audit: true
```

maria gonzalez: love it. One last thing — how do we handle rollbacks? policy versioning + automatic revert if fallback_rate > X for Y minutes? or require manual rollback?

tariq ahmed: automatic revert is dangerous. better: alert + optional auto-pause (only if explicitly enabled in template). Default: notify + open a rollback PR in the policy repo.

maria gonzalez: ok! i'll draft a small RFC with mockups and the YAML schema. tagging @jen, @tariq for review.

jen lee: will review this afternoon. :thumbsup:

samir patel: can we add a tiny demo app that toggles triggers to exercise the dry-run and audit? saves time for QA.

maria gonzalez: yes — i'll include a demo harness in the RFC repo.

kevin chen: if you want, I can wire the evaluate endpoint in staging after deploy-bot finishes.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: policy-service v2.14 -> staging

maria gonzalez: thanks everyone — filing RFC in #eng-platform with link in 20m.

jen lee: thanks!
